comparison: cover crop vs. no cover crop
quote: The topsoil SOC concentration in the LTE treatments was not significantly affected by cover cropping (P = 0.33) neither in conventional or organic cropping systems (Fig. 1a). The SOC concentrations consistently decreased with depth, but there was no significant effect of cover crops at individual depths (25−50 cm, P = 0.26; 50−100 cm, P = 0.33)
note: LTE initiated in 1997; 23 years for organic (OGL) and 15 years for conventional (CGL) systems; no significant effect at any depth to 1 m

comparison: cover crop C input above vs. below threshold
metric: net SOC increase as fraction of added C
quote: In particular, overall C increase equivalent to 20−25% of the added C was achieved, when the cover crop C input was >0.2−0.3 mg C g−1 in the studied soils. These threshold values would correspond to the C input from cover crops with an aboveground yield of about 0.7–1.1 Mg dry matter ha−1
note: Mesocosm study with 14C-labeled fodder radish residues incubated 165 days at 15°C; net SOC increase only occurred above C input threshold in two soils (2.0% and 2.6% SOC)

comparison: cover crop vs. no cover crop
quote: Various meta-analyses have suggested a global potential of cover crops to increase SOC stocks in topsoils (typically defined as the upper 20 or 30 cm soil layer) at rates of 0.3–0.6 Mg carbon (C) ha−1 yr−1 (Poeplau and Don, 2015; Abdalla et al., 2019; Jian et al., 2020).
note: Cited from Poeplau and Don (2015), Abdalla et al. (2019), Jian et al. (2020)
